clue.text: File holders favoured by reluctant judges?

definitions.text: File holders favoured by reluctant judges?

parts.words: File holders favoured by reluctant judges?
parts.note: cases for carrying papers, read whimsically as short trials that a judge who dislikes long hearings would prefer

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of folders judges with little appetite for work might like.
explanation.walkthrough: The bags carry documents; split the word and a lazy judge would favour brief (short) cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Slim attaché bags hold documents, and short court trials are exactly what a reluctant judge would want.

clue.text: Being prepared to study, Spanish girl attends school

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
Ines is a Spanish girl's name

explanation.surface: To get ready to study, a Spanish girl goes to school.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being ready is preparedness, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Aboard old train, regularly call and shout

indicators.note: aboard shows the picked letters are placed inside the other pieces, like passengers

parts.note: ex means former or old
to train a weapon on something is to aim it

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters from the word call

explanation.surface: Someone on an old train regularly calls out and shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway but means AIM; CL (alternate letters of call) goes aboard EX+AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out suddenly with strong feeling is to yell or call out loudly.

clue.text: Criminal -heartless man caught in the act-is sent down

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: caught in shows the shortened man is placed inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word man is removed

explanation.surface: A criminal, a ruthless man caught red-handed, is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: To be sent down is British slang for being jailed; 'heartless' drops the middle letter of man, and 'caught in' places what is left inside the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentenced by a court, especially to prison, is the sense here: found guilty and punished.

clue.text: Rolling Stones noted for inserting line in folksy song

indicators.note: inserting shows the letter for line is put into the rearranged letters
rolling suggests the letters of stones noted for are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones are known for adding a line to a folk tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stones' looks like the band; Rolling is the anagram signal for STONES NOTED FOR, with L inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph McTell's well-known folk ballad about the British capital's poor is a song in this style.

clue.text: Leave ice cream concoction

definitions.meaning: to depart, as in to make a quick exit
a banana dessert topped with ice cream

explanation.surface: Walking out on an elaborate ice cream dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart abruptly is slang for leaving, and the banana dessert with ice cream bears the same word.

clue.text: Black bird in dish

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A dark bird served up in a bowl, like a strange menu item.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded deep container for food is a type of dish.

clue.text: Bill joins in fray, producing sharp-pointed object

indicators.note: joins in shows the bill is put inside the fight

parts.note: a brawl is a fight, a fray
an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill joins a fight and pulls out a sharp tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is AD, an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed hand tool for making holes in wood is a carpenter's spike.

clue.text: Turn with part of foot

parts.note: the heel is the back part of the foot

explanation.surface: Pivoting on the back of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot or rotate round is to swing about, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bistro waiter serving fish and no end of rabbit

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for rabbit is dropped, leaving it without its end

parts.note: cony is an old word for a rabbit

explanation.surface: A French restaurant waiter serves up a dish of fish and most of a rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a male restaurant server is traditionally addressed by this word.

clue.text: Discharged soldiers near area in Leeds surprisingly

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of area plus Leeds turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed near a district of Leeds have been discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' only joins the soldiers to the rest; 'surprisingly' shuffles area's letter together with the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set free or let go from service is to be let out, a synonym.

clue.text: Support a Covent Garden production?

parts.note: aid means support or help

explanation.surface: A request to back a staging at the Royal Opera House.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is the home of London's Royal Opera House; the question mark shows the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera about an Ethiopian princess is an example of a show staged at the Royal Opera House.

clue.text: Union colleague put on uniform in due course

indicators.note: in an across answer, putting one piece on another places the second piece after the first

parts.note: uniform as an adjective means even or regular
TU is the abbreviation for trade union
an ally is an associate or colleague

explanation.surface: A trade unionist's associate will, in time, wear a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like clothing but is an adjective; in an across answer 'put on' places the union and colleague pieces after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening at last, after some time, happens at the proper time eventually: an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: End of trimester?

parts.note: the stopping point of a school term, read as the final station where a line ends

explanation.surface: A question about what comes when a school term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as TERM IN US, a teasing reading of the end of a term; really a railway end station.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stop on a transport line is its end point, with a nod to an academic term.

clue.text: Moles destroyed garden in the end — that's very serious

indicators.note: destroyed indicates that the letters of moles are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
in the end points to the last letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: A gardener grimly reports that moles have ruined their lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' shuffles the moles; 'in the end' takes only the final letter of garden, added last.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and earnest in manner, without levity, is a close synonym.

clue.text: Small role assigned to canine in Australian film

indicators.note: assigned to links the role to the next piece, placing them side by side

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

indicators.note: in shows the canine letter sits inside the Australian abbreviation

parts.note: Aus is an abbreviation for Australian
C stands for canine tooth in dental notation

explanation.surface: A minor part given to a dog in an Australian movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' suggests a dog but is C, the tooth in dental charts; the film is Kubrick's 1960 epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Kubrick's 1960 epic about a slave revolt is a famous movie of this title.

clue.text: Satisfied, having taken single drug

parts.note: to satisfy a need is to meet it, so satisfied gives met
had means taken, as in had a drink
one means single

explanation.surface: Someone content after taking just one dose of a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic opioid used to treat heroin addiction is a medicine and narcotic.

clue.text: Climb a post, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the words are spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it, so this gives A plus SEND

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to climb a pole, as if checking an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a pole to climb but is the verb, to send.
explanation.definitionFit: To go upward is to rise or mount, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Smart walker intended to go outside without hat

indicators.note: to go outside shows the shortened intended word wraps round the walker word
without hat means the top letter of the down answer word is removed

parts.note: meant means intended
a leg is what one walks with

explanation.surface: A well-dressed rambler meant to head out without a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walker' looks like a person but is a body part; 'without hat' removes the top letter of intended, and 'to go outside' wraps what is left round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and refined in appearance is the sense: graceful, well dressed.

clue.text: Strong coffee mother brought in for fellow lodger

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud or strong

indicators.note: brought in shows the word for mother is placed inside the coffee

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone shares a strong coffee with their mother and their housemate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong coffee' looks like one item, but Strong alone is the musical abbreviation; 'brought in' puts mother inside the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares a rented home with you is a co-tenant, the person you room with.

clue.text: Keep track of vehicle crossing province

indicators.note: crossing shows the vehicle spans across the province, enclosing it

parts.note: a motor is a car, a vehicle
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: Tracking a car as it drives across a province.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe and check over time is to watch, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Could it make ailing tot hoarser?

definitions.text: Could it make ailing tot hoarser?

indicators.note: ailing suggests the words tot hoarser are sick and out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent wonders what has made a poorly child's voice croakier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an inflamed throat would make a child croakier.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed pharynx makes the voice rough, which is exactly what would make a child croakier.

clue.text: Knowing no limits, Conservatives left college

indicators.note: knowing no limits signals the outer letters of the party word are removed

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Conservatives with unbounded ambition quit a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Rubbish having nasty smell? That's about right

indicators.note: about shows the smell word goes around the word for right

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a stinking claim as nonsense, then concedes it is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is British slang for a stink; it goes about OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or claptrap is the sense: talk not to be taken seriously.

clue.text: Centre of Nuneaton's well-kept

indicators.note: centre of points to the middle letters of the town name Nuneaton

explanation.surface: Someone praises the tidy middle of Nuneaton, an English Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a town in Warwickshire, England; its middle four letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and orderly means in good order, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Maybe prevented from flying one flag chap had draped round about

indicators.note: the contracted words are draped round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a chap had is he had, contracted to he'd
I is the Roman numeral for one
a jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow, as in Union Jack

explanation.surface: A man has wrapped a flag around something, perhaps grounding an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: A seized plane may be stopped from flying to its destination, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft seized by force may be stopped from continuing its intended journey, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Tree producing fruit-it's gathered by friend mostly

indicators.note: gathered by shows it is taken inside the shortened friend word
mostly signals that the friend word loses its last letter

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
it's gives the word it

explanation.surface: A friend collects most of the fruit from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims the friend's last letter; 'gathered by' places the pronoun inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus tree bearing a large lemon-like fruit is called by this name.

clue.text: Dunce in class test ultimately receiving no marks

indicators.note: receiving shows the zero is taken in between the other pieces

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word test

parts.note: no marks is a score of zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A slow pupil in class scores nothing in the final test.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-witted or foolish person is an idiot, a British colloquial synonym.

clue.text: People who are unhappy about popular TV programme

indicators.note: about shows the unhappy people are placed around the word for popular

parts.note: a misery is a gloomy, complaining person, so these are miseries
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Grumpy viewers moaning about a hit television show.
explanation.walkthrough: A misery is British slang for a habitual moaner; 'about' puts the moaners round the word for popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A short drama serial broadcast in a few episodes is a kind of television show.
